overview.text: The Grass Snake (now often called the Eastern Grass Snake) is a non-venomous snake of Eurasia, usually found near water. In 2017 a DNA study showed that the grass snakes of western Europe are a separate species, the Barred Grass Snake, so the name *Natrix natrix* now covers the populations from Scandinavia and central Europe eastwards.

identification.text: Its most familiar feature is the pale collar behind the head - white or pale yellow.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of Scandinavia and central and eastern Europe, east to Central Asia. Grass snakes in Britain belong to the Barred Grass Snake; records of *N. natrix* there are thought to come from imported animals.

taxonomy.text: A 2017 study in Scientific Reports, using mitochondrial and nuclear DNA, raised the western grass snakes to a species of their own, *Natrix helvetica* (Barred Grass Snake), found from about the Rhine west to the Pyrenees and in Britain. The Iberian and North African grass snakes had already been recognised in 2016 as *N. astreptophora*.

similar.text: the Barred Grass Snake of western Europe, split from it in 2017 using DNA; the two meet and hybridise in contact zones in central Europe.

kindler.title: Hybridization patterns in two contact zones of grass snakes reveal a new Central European snake species

iber.title: Natrix astreptophora (Seoane, 1884) should be recognized as a distinct species
iber.publisher: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
